title_en: The Causes of the Punishment of the Grave
body_ar: ما أفضل عمل للنجاة من عذاب القبر؟ أن عذاب القبر له أسباب تؤدي إليه منها عدم الاستتار من البول، وعدم النظافة منه ومنها المشي بالنميمة ومنها الكذب وغير ذلك كترك أداء الزكاة فهذه الذنوب سبب لعذاب القبر، فإذا كان الإنسان يجتنب هذه الذنوب فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى سينجيه إن شاء من عذاب القبر.
body_en:
What is the best deed for deliverance from the punishment of the grave?

The punishment of the grave has causes that lead to it. Among them is failing to shield oneself from urine and failing to keep clean of it; among them is going about with talebearing (namīmah); among them is lying; and other things besides, such as leaving off the payment of zakat. These sins are a cause of the punishment of the grave. So if a person avoids these sins, God — glorified and exalted is He — will deliver him, if He wills, from the punishment of the grave.

flags.arabic: ما أفضل عمل للنجاة من عذاب القبر؟ ... أن عذاب القبر له أسباب تؤدي إليه
flags.context: the relation of the answer to the question asked
options: publish both as served, with the mismatch noted
publish the answer under the record's own title, which does match it
flags.note: The question asks for the best deed that brings deliverance; the answer instead enumerates the causes of the punishment and concludes that avoiding them brings deliverance. The record's title, 'The Causes of the Punishment of the Grave', matches the answer rather than the question. This is a milder instance of the title/body mismatch recorded at style guide section 11. Both are translated faithfully and neither has been adjusted to fit the other.

flags.context: the ruling status of the acts enumerated
options: render as 'these sins', exactly as given
flags.note: The Sheikh calls these acts sins (dhunūb) and assigns no ruling term to any of them. The English does not supply one. In particular, nothing here is graded forbidden (ḥarām) or disliked (makrūh) in his words, and no such grading may be read into the English.

flags.context: the opening word of the answer
options: read the sentence as beginning with an unelided 'anna' typical of a transcribed oral answer, and render as a plain statement
read a dropped introductory clause before it
flags.note: The answer opens on 'anna' with nothing for it to depend on, which normally indicates either a transcribed spoken answer or a clause lost at the start. The English renders it as a plain statement. If a clause has been lost, it would have been an introductory formula rather than substantive content, since the answer that follows is complete in itself.

translator_notes: A short written fatwa with a complete answer: the Sheikh reaches his own position within the record, so style guide section 10 does not apply and it may be displayed as a fatwa.
'عدم الاستتار من البول' is the classical formulation about guarding against splashes of urine, which is a matter of ritual purity (ṭahārah); rendered plainly rather than euphemistically.
'النميمة' is glossed on first occurrence as talebearing — carrying words between people so as to set them against one another — which is narrower than gossip.
